seoul-culture-itinerary-3-days.alt: Gyeongbokgung and Jongmyo close on Tuesdays. Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung, Deoksugung and Namsangol's houses close on Mondays. Jongmyo, Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung and Deoksugung are free on Wednesdays. Changgyeonggung and Deoksugung stay open to 21:00 from Tuesday to Sunday, and the National Museum of Korea stays open to 21:00 on Wednesdays and Saturdays.
seoul-culture-itinerary-3-days.caption: The week at a glance: which sites close, go free or stay open late on each day.
seoul-culture-itinerary-3-days.basis: drawn from the heritage service, museum and Namsangol pages cited below, checked October 20, 2026.

gyeongbokgung-palace-guide.alt: From south to north on the royal axis: Gwanghwamun main gate, Heungnyemun where tickets are checked, the Yeongjegyo bridge, Geunjeongmun, the Geunjeongjeon throne hall, the Sajeongjeon office, Gangnyeongjeon the king's quarters, Gyotaejeon the queen's residence and the Amisan garden. Gyeonghoeru stands west of Sajeongjeon and Sujeongjeon west of the axis. Bugaksan rises behind.
gyeongbokgung-palace-guide.caption: The royal axis from Gwanghwamun to the Amisan garden, with the two halls that sit west of it.
gyeongbokgung-palace-guide.basis: drawn from the palace pages cited below, checked October 20, 2026; schematic, not to scale.
gyeongbokgung-palace-guide.afterSectionHeading: Why Gyeongbokgung runs in one straight line

seoul-city-wall-hike.alt: Clockwise from Changuimun: Baegak to Hyehwamun, 4.7 km, about 3 hours, hardest; Naksan to Gwanghuimun, 3.2 km, about 1.5 hours, easiest; Namsan to the Donuimun site, 6.7 km, about 3.5 hours, moderate; Inwangsan back to Changuimun, 4.0 km, about 2.5 hours, hard and rocky. The full loop is 18.6 km, about ten and a half hours of walking.
seoul-city-wall-hike.caption: The four official sections as one loop, with the gates where each starts and ends.
seoul-city-wall-hike.basis: drawn from the city's trail pages cited below, checked October 25, 2026; schematic, not to scale.
seoul-city-wall-hike.afterSectionHeading: Four mountains, four very different walks

jjimjilbang-etiquette-guide.alt: Seven steps: put shoes in the shoe locker; pay at the counter for towels, a uniform and a wristband key; undress fully in the single-sex locker room; wash with soap at the showers; use the hot, herbal and cold pools with the towel kept out of the water; put the uniform on for the shared floor with kiln rooms, salt rooms and a snack bar; return the wristband and pay for extras when you leave.
jjimjilbang-etiquette-guide.caption: The order most bathhouses expect, from the shoe locker to returning your wristband.
jjimjilbang-etiquette-guide.basis: drawn from the step list in this guide; rules vary by venue.
jjimjilbang-etiquette-guide.afterSectionHeading: From shoe locker to hot pool: the first fifteen minutes

korean-bbq-ordering-guide.alt: Say 두 명이요 for two people; the table is set; order 삼겹살 1인분, 목살 1인분 주세요; add 소주 한 병이요 for soju; grill and wrap the meat; ask 불판 갈아 주세요 if the plate scorches; finish with 된장찌개하고 공기밥 하나 주세요 for stew and rice or 후식 냉면 하나 주세요 for cold noodles; pay at the counter.
korean-bbq-ordering-guide.caption: Every stage of a pork-barbecue dinner for two, with the phrase to use at each.
korean-bbq-ordering-guide.basis: drawn from the worked order in this guide.
korean-bbq-ordering-guide.afterSectionHeading: A worked order for two at a pork house
